At the secondary ₹88.70 close, approximately 9.45× current-share owner earnings appears inexpensive only if receivables convert and margins hold. GOV.reason: Specific related holdings, compensation and disputed proceedings disclosed; no established critical fraud fail. Noncore group-equity investment, property deal valuation process and restatement presentation defects warrant caution. Disputed 1.2557 tax demand is 5.37% annual group PAT, not existential; group allegations not attributed to issuer.

MOAT.reason: Recurring enterprise integration and multichannel capability support retention. Operator/channel dependence,37.6% largest customer,19.44% churn and usage cancellation limit pricing power; technology label alone is not software moat.

REV.reason: Five-year primary sales 64.63%, parent-only 56.53%, gross contribution 50.74% all above 30% band; organically formed subs and modest restatement cannot change band. Score 9 capped 8 medium confidence for gross operator pass-through/volume price non split. No unsupported quarterly trajectory adjustment.

DUR.reason: Enterprise communications usage and 156.63 crore management-defined recurring revenue support runway. No contracted backlog, high churn/concentration and dependence on funding extended credit limit durable visibility.

CAP.reason: Reported core NOPAT incremental return is strong, and software capex modest relative growth. Persistent receivable funding and noncore MOS allocation mean accounting returns do not establish cash-efficient reinvestment; no high score from ROCE alone.

CASH.reason: Three-year CFO negative 12.83 crore versus PAT 50.22; receivables 50.2% sales and IPO 46 crore WC show persistent funding need. Latest 4.30 positive CFO is counter evidence but not cure; GQ Scap 5.

BAL.reason: Pre IPO debt 9.30 modest versus 90.40 group equity; fresh 49.71 net funds WC. Most assets are debtors, cash 1.74 small and actual post IPO deployment unverified; MOS shares not cash, disputed tax funded internally.

EXEC.reason: Delivered rapid revenue growth, lower churn and organic Dubai initial sales. Cash realization and property/financial documentation process remain weak; forecast WC funding not achieved performance.

EARN.reason: Core profit rises with real gross contribution, other income only 0.76 crore. EBITD A margin fell 12.86% to 11.96%, investment restatement s and low cash realization reduce profit quality; minority and current-share dilution retained.

L.reason: Lot 21.29% position and seven-day median proxy imply 5.16 active-sessions at 5%. Newly listed history too short for reliable 20/60-day liquidity; Oct 13 only 3600 shares and no verified BSE depth/restriction clearance.

R.reason: Material low-confidence inputs are post-IPO customer collections and supplier terms, current proceeds deployment, and the group minority economic allocation. Seven observed trading sessions additionally leave execution risk poorly bounded. These affect achievable return, recoverable downside and the reverse-valuation comparison; absence of calibrated probabilities alone is not the reason for NS.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Dove Soft is a fast-growing enterprise messaging aggregator, not a pure software royalty business. Verified sales and gross contribution growth are strong, but cumulative FY 2024–26 CFO is negative ₹12.83 crore against ₹50.22 crore group PAT. Its IPO chiefly funds extended customer credit. At the secondary ₹88.70 close, approximately 9.45× current-share owner earnings appears inexpensive only if receivables convert and margins hold. This is a cash-conversion-sensitive growth/value watchlist, not a demonstrated compounder. Linked scenarios are provided; IAS remains NS. [S1][S2][S5][S8]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: BSE SME code 544975 / DSL; ISIN INE0NXJ01016; 24,386,755 face-value ₹10 shares. The allotment announcement confirms October 8, 2026 listing. Secondary October 19 close ₹88.70 implies ₹216.31 crore market capitalization. Consolidated FY 2026 includes 92.61%-owned DTL and a new wholly owned Dubai subsidiary. Research assumes five years, a 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh position. G1 has no verified critical fail; G2 has explicit presentation gaps but no critical hold on the reconciled core statements; G3 is Conditional because current proceeds deployment and collections remain uncertain; G4 is Conditional because trading history is short and live depth is unverified. Historical P&L confidence is medium to high, quality-score confidence medium, and valuation/liquidity confidence low. Seven observed sessions are not a 20/60-session sample. A 1,200-share lot costs ₹106,440. [S1][S5][S7][S8]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS is 4. 74. GQS is capped at 5 because CASH 2 reflects persistent weakness. IAS is NS. Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 6, EXEC 5, EARN 4 and L 3. Their claim-linked evidence, weighted contributions, coverage and bounds appear in the audit fields. Missing R/D/P weights are not redistributed. Disputed tax proceedings do not create an unproven G1 failure. [S1]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Clients pay for usage across SMS, voice, Whats App, RCS and email. Dove purchases messaging services from operators and integrates delivery and enterprise interfaces. FY 2026 messaging/direct purchases of ₹223.57 crore consume 81.60% of ₹273.98 crore sales, leaving ₹50.41 crore gross contribution before staff and platform costs. Prepaid or short-payment suppliers and extended-credit customers create structural financing needs. Domestic DTL contributes 18.24% of sales and newly formed Dubai 4.33%. Management-defined annual recurring revenue of ₹156.63 crore reflects recurring usage, not guaranteed subscription backlog. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Integrations and channel relationships provide some operating stickiness. Nevertheless, the largest customer contributes 37.60%, the top ten 79.94%, and the top ten suppliers 92.88%, limiting bargaining power. Customer churn of 19.44%, improved from 23.47% and 29.16%, is still not evidence of a wide moat. Operator price changes, messaging restrictions and customer migration are credible failure modes. Listed communications platforms such as Tan la and Route have different scale, geography and intellectual property; their multiples cannot simply be transplanted. MOAT 4 reflects modest integration benefits rather than a presumed software franchise. [S1]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Primary FY 2021 standalone sales of ₹22.6564 crore to FY 2026 group sales of ₹273.9801 crore imply a 64.63% five-year CAGR. Using only the parent’s FY 2026 ₹212.9005 crore endpoint gives 56.53%. Gross contribution grew from ₹6.4760 crore to ₹50.4099 crore, a 50.74% CAGR. These alternatives all remain above the 30% REV band, bounding the effect of operator pass-through and subsidiary scope. Subsidiaries were organically formed; the issuer reports no business acquisition in the preceding ten years. Group FY 2024/25/26 sales were ₹119.7269/187.7386/273.9801 crore, with annual additions of ₹68.0117 and ₹86.2415 crore. Price/volume separation remains unavailable. The score of 9 implied by the band is capped at 8 for medium confidence. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Usage expansion, additional channels and Dubai support a growth runway, but customer credit rather than factory capacity is the principal reinvestment burden. The ₹46 crore IPO working-capital allocation is planned as ₹22 crore in FY 2027 and ₹24 crore in FY 2028; it is not an asset already earning returns. Projected standalone working capital of ₹86.37/113.75 crore and ₹12 crore borrowings are management estimates, not contracted orders or committed funding. Gross margin slipped to 18.40% from 18.91%, and core EBITDA margin to 11.96% from 12.86%. Reported incremental NOPAT returns are positive, but poor realization prevents high CAP and GQS assessments. [S1][S5]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoters and their group retain 52.86% after the issue; no pledge or convertibles were disclosed at prospectus date. MD remuneration of ₹0.36 crore and two executive directors’ combined ₹0.5235 crore are not the dominant governance concern. More relevant are ₹9.6505 crore invested in related MOS Utility equity while raising working capital, the cancelled-property valuation process, and financial reconciliation presentation defects. The company’s disputed ₹1.2557 crore tax demand is approximately 5.37% of group PAT and must be distinguished from group-company demands. The company contests the assessment; no fraud or guilt inference is made. Consequential public wording requires review. Math i a’s restatement examination differs from the statutory audit by An kush Gupta. Actuarial benefit adjustments and investment valuation changes are disclosed, not automatically malpractice. [S1][S3][S4][S6]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY 2026 owner PAT of ₹22.8875 crore excludes ₹0.5166 crore minority profit. Other income of ₹0.7618 crore is small relative to core EBIT of ₹30.6835 crore. Latest CFO of ₹4.3048 crore less ₹3.8407 crore capex leaves ₹0.4641 crore before deposit advances, but three-year cumulative CFO is negative ₹12.8268 crore. Net debtors of ₹137.6447 crore equal 50.24% of sales; gross amounts over six months are ₹11.2344 crore, including ₹1.1585 crore over three years, against ₹0.5958 crore provision. Provision stock declined despite an expense, requiring a write-off/recovery bridge. FY 2026 original PAT ₹24.3407 crore to restated ₹23.4041 crore and FY 2025 ₹15.7322 crore to ₹16.5400 crore have explicit bridges; equity attribution is less clear. The cash statement reclassifies ₹0.7289 crore unrealized FX through investing, which is not new cash generation. Forecasts start actual note-built WC of ₹81.4233 crore, cash ₹1.7416 crore and debt ₹9.2978 crore. Intangibles of ₹2.4424 crore and development of ₹3.0555 crore still require cash returns. [S1][S4]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹88.70, market capitalization of ₹216.31 crore divided by owner PAT of ₹22.8875 crore gives 9.45× P/E. Using pre-IPO weighted EPS of ₹12.01 would understate it. Five-year bear/base/bull models assume growth of 10/25/40%, EBITDA margins of 7/11/13%, WC ratios of 38/30/25% and terminal EV/EBITDA of 6/9/12×. They use actual March balances and add the conservative ₹49.708 crore net IPO proceeds once in FY 2027. Only changes in WC are charged, not a second ₹46 crore expense. Debt deficits accrue assumed 12% interest; capex is 1.5% of revenue, depreciation 0.8%, and additional collateral 2% of revenue growth. Terminal group equity deducts debt and a ₹3.708 crore GCP reserve before an explicitly approximate 2.21% minority economic deduction. MOS shares and miscellaneous loan recoveries have zero assumed terminal recovery. The terminal prices are approximately ₹80.02/353.08/954.62, with IR Rs −2.04%/31.82%/60.84%. These widely separated conditional cases are not calibrated probabilities or a buy range. [S1][S5][S8] Financing timing update: interest now uses opening gross debt plus half-year draws less half-year repayments, solved with cash tax and funding. Revised bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹80.02, ₹353.08, ₹954.62; corresponding five-year returns are -2.04%, 31.82%, 60.84%. These replace opening-only-interest outputs; no borrowing availability is implied.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The permanent-loss path is a major customer reducing usage or extending credit while suppliers shorten payment terms. Receivables then grow or become impaired, IPO cash is exhausted, and new debt or dilution combines with a lower exit multiple. The severe model assumes 10% annual revenue contraction, 4% EBITDA margin, 45% WC, an additional loss equal to 15% of opening debtors and a 4× terminal multiple. Financing availability is assumed, not guaranteed. Neither MOS shares nor book debtors establish a recovery floor. Counter evidence includes real gross-contribution growth, lower churn, modest starting debt and fresh equity. Tax risk is assessed separately rather than treated as proof of business fraud. [S1][S5] Impairment is a noncash opening-asset loss. The model reduces usable opening working capital and includes replacement funding once in delta WC, rather than treating a write-off as a separate cash payment; any contingent tax/legal settlement remains a separate cash item.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5× requires 37.97% annual per-share appreciation; 10× requires 58.49%. Historical sales growth of 64.63% exceeds both, but gross-contribution growth of 50.74%, share dilution and negative cumulative cash prevent a direct inference about shareholder returns. High growth must become collectible earnings without repeated external capital, and an appropriate terminal multiple must survive. The base/bull models show conditional requirements, not probabilities. No 5× or 10× recommendation is established. [S1][S2][S5]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor actual ₹46 crore WC deployment against the ₹22/24 crore schedule; collections on ₹137.6447 crore debtors and ₹11.2344 crore over six months; repeat CFO and repair of the three-year ₹12.8268 crore deficit; largest-customer concentration of 37.60% and churn of 19.44%; gross/EBITDA margins of 18.40/11.96%; returns on ₹3.0555 crore software development; allocation to ₹9.6505 crore MOS shares and further connected investments; tax appeals and the property-valuation clarification without assuming their outcomes; post-IPO shareholding/pledges; and at least 20/60 observed sessions plus live BSE conditions before improving liquidity confidence. [S1][S5][S7][S8]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: cash-conversion-sensitive growth/value watchlist, not a compounder. Quality scores have medium confidence and GQS is capped at 5; IAS remains unrankable until repeat collections and adequate trading evidence support its inputs. A low P/E cannot by itself resolve asset-quality and allocation risks. Disputed allegations or the small objects-table difference do not establish a critical integrity failure. Reassessment requires current collections and deployment, clearer financial bridges and practical execution liquidity. No public write or trade was performed.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The issuer’s October 5 final prospectus and allotment take precedence over earlier drafts and secondary claims of a ₹111 issue price; the verified final price is ₹110. Scanned FY 2021/25 annuals and original consolidated statements were reviewed, and financial notes F 13–15 visually checked. The 24,386,755 share count agrees with the official master. Remaining gaps include post-IPO deployment, the original FY 2026 annual not found in the reviewed directory, complete equity/provision roll-forwards, updated appeal outcomes and missing listing-day OHLCV. Copying/date errors and the ₹0.1279 crore objects discrepancy are not inflated into critical failures. Forecasts explicitly use actual opening WC and fresh capital only once. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S8][S9]
